description: Slowloris-style attack against an externally-launched HTTP/1.1 target. N concurrent TCP connections open, each writing a partial request header byte-by-byte with a sleep between bytes; never sends the final CRLF CRLF that completes the headers. PRIMARY CHECK: after attack_duration_seconds + cooldown_seconds, target serves clean GET /health with 200 OK within max_response_ms. SECONDARY CHECK: process RSS delta within rss_growth_pct_max (no leaked connection state).
loopback_caveat: Loopback can mask socket-buffer effects relative to network paths. transport_mode=loopback-h1 mandatory.

attack_profile.note: Bumping connection_count >= the target's max-connections limit is the point of the test. The harness does NOT enforce a cap; pick connection_count according to the target's configured limit.

tolerance.rss_note: rss_growth_pct_max is measured against a baseline taken AFTER a warm-up (baseline_warmup_seconds in the artifact). Before 2026-08-26 the baseline was cold, so first-load JIT, metaspace fill and heap commit were charged to the attack: the first slowloris run read +34.9 % against this 5 % bound while its JFR put live heap after the forced GC at 9.5 MB. RSS remains a weak leak signal here -- see comparison_axis_note -- and a run without NMT leaves the non-heap remainder unattributed. Do not compare rss_bytes_delta across runs with different baseline_warmup_seconds. Both samples are additionally preceded by a forced GC (since 2026-08-27), so the delta compares two post-collection states -- retained memory. Before that date only the FINAL sample was, which compared a collected heap against an uncollected one and biased the delta toward understating growth; on destructive-radamsa-h2 it read -588 517 376 bytes. Artifacts from before that change are not comparable with later ones.
tolerance.hang_note: hang_count is 0 by construction here: this driver holds connections open deliberately and has no per-request deadline of its own, so it has nothing to report as a hang. Until 2026-08-27 the runner mapped the attacker's connections_dropped onto hang_count and passed it to the classifier as the hang argument, which INVERTS the scenario -- evicting a half-open connection is the defence against slowloris, so a target doing the right thing would have been recorded as hanging and pushed toward a degraded class. The first run scored connections_dropped: 0, so the inversion produced hang_count: 0 and stayed hidden.
tolerance.connections_note: connections_dropped is the measurement this scenario exists to make, not a failure it gates on: it counts how many half-open connections the TARGET closed during the window. It also licenses the incomplete-wait outcome in the radamsa drivers -- a target that evicts none inside 120 s cannot have been the source of a 2 s attacker-side timeout. What this scenario gates on is liveness and the RSS delta.

comparison_axis_note: Cross-stack slowloris results are NOT comparable without explicit normalization of (a) max-concurrent-connections, (b) header-receive-timeout, (c) idle-connection-eviction interval. Different runtimes have different defaults; comparison without normalizing these is apples-to-oranges. Label connection_count, header_delay_seconds, attack_duration_seconds in any cross-stack report row.
